name: Onesimus
overview: Onesimus was a male Colossian recognized by the Apostle Paul as a faithful and beloved brother, highlighting a close spiritual bond. Paul sent Onesimus back to Philemon, indicating a significant role in the early Christian community and a personal connection between these believers. His identity as a Colossian situates him within the church addressed in the epistle to the Colossians.
namesAndTitles: The name Onesimus appears once in Scripture without a recorded meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as his proper name, with no additional title or significance indicated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Onesimus beyond his designation as Paul's faithful and beloved brother. There are no other familial connections noted in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Onesimus holds importance in the New Testament as a figure who embodies Christian transformation and fellowship, evidenced by Paul's affectionate description of him. His return to Philemon at Paul's instruction underscores themes of reconciliation and Christian responsibility within the early church. Through Onesimus, the epistle to Philemon addresses practical applications of the gospel in interpersonal relationships.
